heading: Claude 3.5 Haiku plans rhyme endings before writing the line
definition: when writing rhyming verse, the model represents candidate rhyme words before writing the line, and intervening on them changes the line to fit a different ending.
summary: The original illustration shows advance rhyme planning and changed endings after internal interventions in Claude 3.5 Haiku. The supplied evidence contains no independent reproduction or aggregate success rates.

suggested_status.by_scale: R0 at an unstated size: Claude 3.5 Haiku only (counts: versions.V1.studies_by_size = {not stated: 1}). No V1 test at toy, <1B, 1-10B, 10-100B or >100B as the counts bucket sizes.
suggested_status.reason: Counts identify the original companion post lw:zsr4rWRASxwmgXfmq as the only V1-tested study: versions.V1.studies_tested = 1; versions.V1.original_sources_linked. Counts also record versions.V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 0, versions.V1.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 0 and versions.V1.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0; these are corpus metadata, not claims established by the post. The original illustrates a couplet in Claude 3.5 Haiku: the untreated ending is rabbit (lw:zsr4rWRASxwmgXfmq#r1), suppressing rabbit produces habit (lw:zsr4rWRASxwmgXfmq#r2), and injecting green produces the nonrhyming ending green (lw:zsr4rWRASxwmgXfmq#r3). The untreated comparison is explicit; no additional control protocol, aggregate rates or uncertainty estimates are reported. Counts: versions.V1.rows_by_evidence_form.text = 3; versions.V1.tested_with_uncertainty = 0; versions.V1.tested_with_code = 0. R0 reflects the original illustrated setting without independent reproduction in these records.
suggested_status.open_questions:
Each of these results would change the level:
- R1: the original authors extend the suppression and injection results to more prompts or other Claude models, with rates.
- R2: a group other than the original's reproduces the trace and the interventions (ideally T1: same method and measure) on a frontier model, ideally from another family.
- C: a failed replication, or an argument that the examples are artifacts of the intervention method.
Two further questions stay open. First, whether the V4 studies on open models (counts: versions.V4.studies_tested = 3, versions.V4.studies_with_challenges = 2) should bear on V1. As worded, V1 is limited to a frontier model. Second, whether a fuller report with numbers exists for the original method: the pack's recipe line says the post leaves out the method details.

source.title: Tracing the Thoughts of a Large Language Model

original_result.setup: The study traced and intervened on Claude 3.5 Haiku’s internal activity while it composed a second line following “grab it”.
original_result.result: The model represented “rabbit” before starting the second line; suppressing that concept changed the ending to “habit”. Injecting “green” produced a sensible line ending in “green” that no longer rhymed.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

r1 reports one planned word, "rabbit", represented before the second line starts. r2 reports that after "rabbit" is suppressed, the line ends in "habit". No row reports more than one candidate being measured as represented at the same time.

wording_issues.phrase: intervening on them changes the line to fit a different ending
wording_issues.issue: Suppressing the planned candidate "rabbit" gives a line ending in "habit", which still rhymes (r2). Injecting "green", which is not a rhyme candidate, gives a line ending in "green" that does not rhyme (r3; the header's method-sensitivity line). The verdict fix on r3 changed its state from partial to observed for V1. The statement leaves two things open: whether the new ending must still rhyme, and whether the intervention must target a candidate rhyme word ('them') or may add an unrelated concept.

method_sensitivity.factor: Type of intervention and concept used: suppressing the planned rhyme word vs injecting an unrelated concept
method_sensitivity.what: On Claude 3.5 Haiku, for the second line after a line ending in "grab it": the untreated line ends in "rabbit" (r1); suppressing the "rabbit" concept gives a line ending in "habit" (r2); injecting the "green" concept gives a line ending in "green" that does not rhyme (r3). These are the original source's own illustrative examples on one couplet, with an explicit untreated comparison. No aggregate rates, uncertainty estimates or additional control protocol are reported.
